page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-60-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine designed for balanced compute, memory, and high-speed local storage throughput. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 60 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 30 physical cores with two threads per core. System memory totals 240 GB, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Storage is bundled with 1,608 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity across four drives, while graphics acceleration is not included.

Benchmark results show strong parallel execution capabilities across dense multi-core workloads. The instance achieves top-quartile performance in stress-ng multi-core testing (86,095.98), Geekbench multi-core scoring (17,718.0), and Clang software compilation (50,016.0). Cryptographic acceleration is reinforced by native AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, reflected in a top-tier PassMark encryption score of 67,128.37. Single-threaded throughput is moderately paced, with Geekbench single-core scoring in the middle 50% tier at 1,875.0, balanced by a strong stress-ng single-core metric of 2,864.57.

In data-intensive benchmarks, the server demonstrates high throughput for distributed in-memory and disk operations. It registers 78.94 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and scores 26,706.5 in PassMark database operations, both placing in the top 25%. Cached memory read throughput is significant at 4,247.26 GB/sec, though uncached large-block reads and writes operate at an average 146.58 GB/sec and 52.61 GB/sec respectively. Small-model LLM prompt processing delivers 3,055.27 tokens per second, but throughput tapers to average tiers when handling large parameter models without dedicated accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the bundled 1.6 TB of local NVMe SSD storage combined with 60 dedicated AMD EPYC cores eliminates external network storage latency and supplementary provisioning overhead for IOPS-sensitive applications. However, instances requiring solely compute without local scratch space may encounter unused storage resources. The server is suited for high-transaction relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, large-scale CI/CD compilation pipelines, and transactional ETL workflows.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-60-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine configured with 60 dedicated vCPUs across 30 physical AMD EPYC 9B14 cores on the x86_64 architecture, 240 GB of RAM, and 1,608 GB of local NVMe SSD storage across four drives. It maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM allocation and contains no GPU accelerators. The instance exhibits top-tier multi-threaded compute, Clang compilation speed, and cryptographic processing, alongside a strong Redis throughput of 78.94 million operations per second and high database operational scores. While uncached memory bandwidth and single-core execution align with median cloud averages, the high density of dedicated cores and integrated low-latency NVMe storage deliver strong resource consolidation for I/O-intensive workloads. The instance is suited for multi-threaded database systems, high-throughput caching, CI/CD build farms, and batch analytics.
